locator: §5.2, 'some semantic theorists have proposed that all that is needed to have minimal truth conditions is for a set of judgments to satisfy two constraints'
interpretation: The minimalist sufficiency conditions (Boghossian 1990, Wright 1993, Divers and Miller 1994): (1) the surface syntax of paradigmatic truth-apt sentences, with grammatical embedding in conditionals and attitude ascriptions; (2) disciplined use, with clearly appropriate and inappropriate conditions of use. Read as: meeting both suffices for minimal truth-aptness. Only sufficiency is formalized ('all that is needed'), not necessity. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
